candidates.source_attribution: Cyril of Alexandria, Commentary on Luke, Homily CXXXI (R. Payne Smith trans., 1859). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Luke (c. 430 AD)

On the Temple-elders' challenge 'by what authority doest thou these things?' (Lk 20:1-2), Cyril reads the authority-question as the canonical Lukan anchor of the doctrine that Christ's authority is self-authenticating, not derived from human institutions: the Lord refuses to license his actions to the question-form because to do so would already concede that authority is delegable by the Sanhedrin. Christ's counter-question about John's baptism (Lk 20:4) traps the elders in their own institutional logic. Tewahedo ecclesial theology cites Lk 20:1-8 as the canonical Lukan anchor of the doctrine that the Church's authority traces to Christ directly, not through Imperial-Sanhedrin-style human delegation.

Cyril of Alexandria Commentary on Luke (c. 430 AD)

On the parable of the wicked husbandmen (Lk 20:9-16), Cyril reads the vineyard-tenants who reject the servants and finally kill the heir as the canonical Lukan anchor of the salvation-history-as-progressive-rejection: prophets sent, prophets killed; finally the Son sent, the Son killed; the vineyard given to others (Gentiles + Tewahedo). The 'heir' language is Christological: Christ's death is the prophetic-final rejection that opens the vineyard to the wider mission. Tewahedo missionary-theology cites Lk 20:9-16 + Mt 21:43 ('the kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof') as the canonical doubled-witness for the doctrine that the Gentile-Ethiopian inclusion in the vineyard is the consequence of the canonical-prophetic rejection of Christ at Calvary.
